message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**. It’s a young, massive gas‑giant orbiting the star HD 100546 and has a radius roughly 2½–3 times that of Jupiter (about 2.5 R_J). Its mass is estimated to be around 10–20 M_J, making it one of the most massive planets ever found.

It’s worth noting that our census of exoplanets is still incomplete—there could be even larger planets out there that we haven’t detected yet, especially if they’re farther from their stars or have unusual orbital inclinations. For now, though, HD 100546 b holds the record among confirmed exoplanets.
